record.context_brief: Counting Hamiltonian cycles in cubic bipartite graphs
record.original_question: Does there exist a 3-connected cubic bipartite graph that has exactly four Hamiltonian cycles?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.4. Does there exist a 3-connected cubic bipartite graph having precisely 4 Hamiltonian cycles?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graph is called cubic if every vertex has degree exactly 3. A graph is bipartite if its vertex set can be partitioned into two independent sets. A graph is 3-connected if it has at least 4 vertices and remains connected after the removal of any 2 vertices. A Hamiltonian cycle in a graph is a cycle that visits every vertex exactly once.

It is known that every cubic bipartite graph has an even number of Hamiltonian cycles, and (when Hamiltonian) has at least 4 Hamiltonian cycles.

Question: Does there exist a 3-connected cubic bipartite graph that has precisely 4 Hamiltonian cycles?
artifact.category_tag: Hamiltonian cycles in cubic bipartite graphs
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up an explicit resolution of the question of whether a 3-connected cubic bipartite graph with exactly 4 Hamiltonian cycles exists. Related literature treats Hamiltonicity of 3-connected cubic bipartite (and bipartite planar) graphs and lower bounds on the number of Hamiltonian cycles in cubic bipartite graphs, but does not appear to settle the precise-count question.

status_evidence.title: Hamiltonian cubic bipartite graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Hamiltonicity and complexity of Hamiltonian cycle problem in cubic bipartite graphs but does not address exact count of 4 Hamiltonian cycles.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the precise-count question found in this related work.

status_evidence.title: Hamiltonian cycles in cubic 3-connected bipartite planar graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Hamiltonicity of 3-connected cubic bipartite planar graphs (Barnette's conjecture context).
status_evidence.claim: Related results on existence rather than exact enumeration.
